income_tax_rates_credits_2026.label: Income tax standard rate cut-off point and PAYE/Personal credits, single person, 2026
income_tax_rates_credits_2026.value: 20% up to EUR 44,000 standard rate cut-off point, 40% above; Personal Tax Credit EUR 2,000 and Employee (PAYE) Tax Credit EUR 2,000, both held at 2025 levels in Budget 2026
income_tax_rates_credits_2026.source_name: KPMG Ireland, Budget 2026 tax rates and credits tables (aggregating Revenue Commissioners / Budget 2026 figures)

usc_rates_bands_2026.label: Universal Social Charge (USC) rates and bands, 2026
usc_rates_bands_2026.value: Full exemption if total income <= EUR 13,000; otherwise 0.5% to EUR 12,012, 2% to EUR 28,700 (widened from EUR 27,382 in Budget 2026), 3% to EUR 70,044, 8% above
usc_rates_bands_2026.source_name: KPMG Ireland, Budget 2026 tax rates and credits tables

prsi_class_a_2026.label: PRSI Class A rates and thresholds, January-September 2026
prsi_class_a_2026.value: Employee: exempt at or below EUR 352/week; tapering PRSI credit up to EUR 12/week phased out linearly between EUR 352.01 and EUR 424/week; 4.2% of full weekly earnings above the taper zone. Employer: 9.0% of full weekly earnings at or below EUR 496/week, 11.25% above.
prsi_class_a_2026.source_name: KPMG Ireland, Budget 2026 tax rates and credits tables, cross-checked against income.ie PRSI guidance
prsi_class_a_2026.note: A further increase (employee 4.35%, employer reduced/standard 9.15%/11.40%, reduced-rate threshold raised to EUR 552/week) is scheduled from 1 October 2026 as part of a multi-year phased increase agreed in prior budgets. This module uses the January-September 2026 rates as the single annual reference, consistent with how other modules in this project pick one effective-date snapshot per year.

national_minimum_wage_2026.label: National Minimum Wage (age 20 and over) from 1 January 2026
national_minimum_wage_2026.source_name: Government of Ireland / Low Pay Commission, Budget 2026

full_time_hours_convention.label: 39 hours/week as the most commonly cited Irish full-time benchmark
full_time_hours_convention.note: Ireland has no single statutory full-time weekly-hours figure (the Organisation of Working Time Act 1997 sets only a 48-hour maximum average); 39h/week is the most frequently cited standard full-time convention.

ppp_conversion_factor.label: PPP conversion factor, households and NPISHs final consumption expenditure (LCU per international $), Ireland, 2024
